title: SAL-01 Lead-to-Order Conversion: declared formula, numerator and denominator with honest missing-data behaviour
risk: The Lead-to-Order Conversion figure is produced under different accounting rules - paid orders divided by all leads, which mixes the marketing lead base into the sales denominator - so the KPI is wrong in the direction that flatters the programme and every decision taken on it inherits the error.
preconditions: Namespace gov-kpi-<case_id>-<worker_id>; the metric is computed by the real reporting code over fixtures/offline/governance.json kpi_dataset and never copied from the dashboard payload.

Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z with the reporting window 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z .. 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z as a half-open interval; the stored aggregate is recomputed independently from the raw counter rows.
Metric scope is fixed before measurement: numerator is orders completed with confirmed payment; denominator is qualified leads advised by the Sales Agent in the window.
The dictionary entry for 'Lead-to-Order Conversion' (owner, unit, window, exclusion rule) is loaded read-only and is compared with the recomputation instead of being trusted.

inputs.formula: paid orders divided by qualified leads advised in the same observation window
inputs.wrong_value_if_buggy: paid orders divided by all leads, which mixes the marketing lead base into the sales denominator
inputs.expected_boundary_behaviour: no advised lead in the window returns NOT_DEFINED

steps.action: Compute Lead-to-Order Conversion from the frozen rows in kpi_dataset.sales
steps.expected: The stored aggregate reports 20.0% and records the formula, the window and the currency that produced it.

steps.action: Recompute Lead-to-Order Conversion independently from the raw counter rows for the same tenant and window
steps.expected: The recomputed value equals the stored value 20.0%, and every numerator row lies inside the denominator scope.

steps.action: Force the empty-source variant of the metric (no qualifying row in the window)
steps.expected: The metric reports no advised lead in the window returns NOT_DEFINED; the display distinguishes missing source data from a measured zero.

steps.action: Read the dashboard payload and the metric dictionary entry
steps.expected: The dashboard renders the stored value with its window, coverage and source, and the dictionary names the owner, unit, numerator and denominator that the recomputation used.

assertions: Lead-to-Order Conversion equals 20.0% for the frozen window, recomputed from the raw counter rows with numerator scope 'orders completed with confirmed payment' and denominator scope 'qualified leads advised by the Sales Agent in the window'.

A recomputation that yields paid orders divided by all leads, which mixes the marketing lead base into the sales denominator is detected as wrong: the stored aggregate and the independent recomputation must agree before the figure is published.
The dashboard payload for the same tenant and window carries the stored value with its window, coverage and measurement source; it substitutes neither a design target nor another metric's value.
Boundary behaviour: no advised lead in the window returns NOT_DEFINED; missing source data is never rendered as a measured zero.
forbidden: Counting an unpaid or cancelled order as a converted order.
Widening the denominator to the whole lead base.
evidence: Paid order list with the payment confirmation timestamps.
Advised-lead log from the Sales Agent.
cleanup: Delete gov- aggregate, raw-counter and scenario rows for SAL-01 after exporting the recomputation table.
automation: The reporting service and the metric dictionary run as real code under test over the frozen KPI dataset; the dashboard is a consumer whose displayed value must equal the independently recomputed value. Waits are condition-based on the stored aggregate row, metric values are never supplied as inputs, and no vendor boundary is involved in the arithmetic.
